row.Consumer complaint narrative:
Our US Bank Line of Credit is showing up on our report as if we pay it late. When in fact we have NOT used that account in several years. What happened is in late XXXX US Bank had a security breach where someone got into our US Bank checking/savings account and performed fraudulent transactions. Since the bank did not catch it ... they took it upon themselves to use the line of credit to cover the money/purchases that was being stolen. We called them multiple times when we noticed the money coming out of our checking/savings account and also let them know they should not be using the " inactive '' line of credit to cover these unauthorized charges that were a breach of their system. Once they took it upon themselves to use the line of credit to cover unauthorized transactions, they would then charge us interest on that line. It took weeks for them to reconcile the unauthorized charges and correct their inappropriate use of our line of credit to cover those transactions. It was known that we would not make payments to that line of credit because WE did not utilize the line of credit and wanted to make sure they corrected every transaction and were not attempting to charge us interest on the line of credit to cover the fraudulent checking/savings account transactions. It appears the bank did not record these weeks of conversations in their system because they are showing up on our credit report as if we made late payments to our line of credit. When in fact it was their delay in researching the fraud and correcting the balance amounts across the checking/savings account and the line of credit. 

This US Bank Line of Credit mark on our credit needs to be corrected. If you research the transaction history you can see we had not used that line of credit for years and their should be a record of the fraudulent activity on our checking/savings account that show that US Bank ( not us ) accessed the line of credit so any late " payment '' to that account was their late payment ... no ours because we did not use the line of credit and did not do the transactions that bank tried to cover with our line.

row.Consumer complaint narrative:
On XXXX XXXX XXXX received an e-mail from XXXX XXXX XXXX from Nationstar Mortgage stating they needed an updated award letter for my XXXX payments so they could complete my request for a modification.. I sent the document back by e-mail on the XXXX of XXXX. 
On the XXXX XXXX at XXXX I received a call from Nationstar stating that request for modification had been denied on the XXXX and that my house was in active forclosure but a sale date had not been set yet. I could avoid it by sending them {$62000.00}. 

Today at XXXXI received another call stating the same thing except the caller wanted {$54000.00}. This caller told me she was calling from the XXXX 's, no wonder we can never get ahold of our dedicated loan specialist. 

Since I was still engaged in my request for a modification on the XXXX of XXXX, How could they have gone through all the legal requirements in two days to have my house in active forclosure status, and be scheduling a sale? 
I believe that this an abusive tactic from Nationstar in violation The New Jersey Fair Debt Collection Act bill # S410 and the federal Fair Debt Collection Practices Act Pub L.95-109. 

I believe that this is an ongoing practice of this company and since they record all their phone calls they should be able to supply you with a transcript of these calls. 

This company should be investigated into their business practices and be made to be held accountable. 

I am in the process of contacting an attorney to initiate civil action against this company.
